walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecosystems, Biodiversity & Management — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecosystems, Biodiversity & Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecosystems, Biodiversity & Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between glacial abrasion and plucking?
options: Abrasion: rock embedded in the glacier base scrapes the bedrock smooth, creating striations. Plucking: meltwater refreezes onto bedrock, then movement rips chunks of rock away.
Outsourcing means moving to another country and offshoring means hiring contractors.
Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.
Abrasion and plucking are different words for the same process.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between outsourcing and offshoring?
options: Outsourcing means moving to another country and offshoring means hiring contractors.
Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.

Outsourcing means contracting work to another company; offshoring means relocating work to another country. A firm can outsource without offshoring, or offshore without outsourcing (in-house overseas).
Outsourcing and offshoring are the same thing.
